skill.name: stitch-loop
skill.description: Guides AI agents through iterative website creation with Stitch, using baton files, site context, and design system prompts.
skill.summary: Builds multi-page Stitch websites through an iterative baton workflow.
skill.author: google-labs-code

security_audit.summary: Most static findings are false positives caused by Markdown backticks, template examples, a localhost URL, and optional local screenshot capture. One real external command risk remains because the skill suggests running npx through Bash for preview, and semantic review found risks from untrusted baton content and an autonomous continuation loop. No evidence found of credential theft, hidden exfiltration, or malicious payloads.

remediation.issue: Baton and site documents can steer agent actions.
remediation.suggestion: Treat next-prompt.md, SITE.md, and DESIGN.md as untrusted input; validate filenames, reject unexpected tool requests, and restrict writes to queue and site/public.

remediation.issue: The loop can continue work without an explicit stop gate.
remediation.suggestion: Add a documented maximum iteration count or require human approval before CI, agent chains, or scheduled runs continue to the next baton.

remediation.issue: The preview step uses Bash with npx to start a local server.
remediation.suggestion: Require user confirmation before running the command, prefer a pinned local dependency, and document how to stop the server cleanly.

remediation.issue: Generated assets are retrieved from Stitch download URLs.
remediation.suggestion: Verify that download URLs come from the expected Stitch tool response and save assets only inside the project queue directory.

```markdown

Parse `next-prompt.md` to extract:

3. **Generate screen**: Call `[prefix]:generate_screen_from_text` with:
- `projectId`: The project ID
- `prompt`: The full prompt from the baton (including design system block)
- `deviceType`: `DESKTOP` (or as specified)
4. **Retrieve assets**: Call `[prefix]:get_screen` to get:
- `htmlCode.downloadUrl` — Download and save as `queue/{page}.html`
- `screenshot.downloadUrl` — Download and save as `queue/{page}.png`

4. **Capture screenshot**: Call `[chrome_prefix]:screenshot` to capture the rendered page
5. **Visual comparison**: Compare against the Stitch screenshot (`queue/{page}.png`) for fidelity

semantic_findings.title: Untrusted Baton Content Drives Agent Actions
semantic_findings.description: The skill tells agents to parse next-prompt.md prompt content and use it to call Stitch tools and write generated pages. A malicious baton or SITE file could steer tool calls and file writes unless these project files are treated as untrusted input.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The workflow explicitly converts file content into prompts and tool calls, and the example SITE file contains direct agent instructions. The risk depends on repository trust, so confidence is high but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Autonomous Loop Persists Work Items
semantic_findings.description: The skill requires updating next-prompt.md before completion and the example project rules say to keep the loop moving. In CI or agent-chain use, this can sustain repeated modifications without a built-in approval gate.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The persistence behavior is an explicit design goal and is documented in both the core skill and example rules. The actual impact depends on how an operator triggers the loop.

content.value_statement: Multi-page Stitch projects can lose context between agent runs. This skill keeps site goals, design rules, generated pages, and the next task organized through a baton workflow.
actual_capabilities: Reads a next-prompt.md baton file to identify the next page and Stitch prompt.
Uses Stitch MCP tools to create projects, generate screens, and retrieve generated assets.
Stages generated HTML and screenshots in a queue before moving pages into site/public.
Updates SITE.md to track completed pages, roadmap items, and remaining ideas.
Writes the next baton task so the workflow can continue across agent runs.
Optionally uses Chrome DevTools to compare rendered pages against Stitch screenshots.
limitations: Requires a configured Stitch MCP server and access to the target Stitch project.
Depends on accurate SITE.md and DESIGN.md files for consistent output.
Does not provide a full build system, deployment pipeline, or hosting configuration.
Optional visual verification requires Chrome DevTools MCP and a local dev server.

use_cases.title: Extend a Product Site
use_cases.description: Generate the next planned page, merge it into navigation, and update the roadmap after review.

use_cases.title: Prototype a Design System
use_cases.description: Reuse DESIGN.md guidance so several generated pages share one visual language.

use_cases.title: Manage Agent Handoffs
use_cases.description: Keep the current task, completed pages, and next iteration documented for repeated AI-assisted work.

prompt_templates.title: Run the Next Baton
prompt_templates.prompt: Read next-prompt.md, generate the requested Stitch page, place the output in site/public, update SITE.md, and write the next baton.

prompt_templates.title: Continue the Roadmap
prompt_templates.prompt: Use SITE.md and DESIGN.md to pick the highest priority unfinished page, generate it with Stitch, and prepare the next roadmap task.

prompt_templates.title: Verify Visual Fidelity
prompt_templates.prompt: Generate the baton page with Stitch, run a local preview if available, compare it with the Stitch screenshot, and fix visible layout issues.

prompt_templates.title: Operate a Controlled Loop
prompt_templates.prompt: Run one Stitch loop iteration only. Validate the baton filename, restrict writes to queue and site/public, document changes, and stop for review.

output_examples.input: A baton asks for a contact page using the current design system.
output_examples.output: The agent generates a contact page, adds it to site/public, marks it complete in SITE.md, and prepares the next page task.

output_examples.input: SITE.md lists a sustainability page as the next high priority item.
output_examples.output: The agent creates a sustainability page prompt, uses Stitch to generate the screen, and records the new page in the sitemap.

output_examples.input: Chrome DevTools MCP is available after generation.
output_examples.output: The agent opens the local page, captures a screenshot, compares it to the Stitch reference, and notes any visual fixes made.

best_practices: Review next-prompt.md before each run and reject unexpected instructions or unsafe filenames.
Keep SITE.md and DESIGN.md current so generated pages follow the same structure and style.
Run one iteration at a time when using CI or agent chains, then review the diff.
anti_patterns: Do not let a baton request write outside the project page and queue directories.
Do not run the loop unattended against untrusted repository content.
Do not skip visual review when generated pages contain navigation, forms, or important layout changes.

faq.question: What is the baton file?
faq.answer: next-prompt.md stores the current page request and the instructions that the next agent run should use.

faq.question: Does this skill require Stitch MCP?
faq.answer: Yes. The workflow depends on Stitch MCP tools for project creation, screen generation, and asset retrieval.

faq.question: Can it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code when the needed tools are available.

faq.question: Does it deploy websites?
faq.answer: No. It organizes generated pages in the repository, but hosting and deployment remain separate tasks.

faq.question: How does it keep styles consistent?
faq.answer: It tells the agent to copy design system guidance from DESIGN.md into each Stitch generation prompt.

faq.question: What should I review before running it?
faq.answer: Review next-prompt.md, SITE.md, DESIGN.md, and any generated file changes before continuing the loop.
